# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Top picks**

| Need | Pick | Price (from sources) |
|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (down from $299) |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $180 list, about $125 at some retailers |
| Best for long runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 |
| Best budget | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $79.99 at Amazon, per SoundGuys |
| Cheapest way to try the style | JLab Flex Open | about $40-50 |

**Why these**

- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** are Runner's World's best overall. They have excellent audio quality, a comfortable clip design, and little sound leakage. They have physical buttons, which WIRED says are easier to use while running than touch controls. Battery is about 7 hours, or 19.5 with the case, and they are only IPX4, so they are weaker in heavy rain. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new pair of open-ear earbuds within about a month, so you may want to wait. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** is the best choice if hearing your surroundings is your top priority. It has 12 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, and physical controls. WIRED says it has bigger bass but a bit less clarity than the older OpenRun. The neckband can interfere with low ponytails and hoods. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/). RTINGS rates the Bose slightly better for most people, but notes that the Shokz is tougher and pairs with multiple devices. [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- **Shokz OpenDots 2** is WIRED's best open earbud overall. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, and it stayed secure and comfortable in WIRED's testing. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2** is SoundGuys' budget pick. It has IP55 protection and long battery life. One retailer listing gives 10 hours per bud and 42 with the case. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
  - **Buy:** [Soundcore AeroFit 2](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) is listed at $129.99, or about $104 with code AFSC20 (last tested 2026-10-22, full-price items only). That is an affiliate link, and Dealectric is paid if you buy. SoundGuys shows $79.99 at Amazon, so compare before buying.
- **JLab Flex Open** is a low-risk way to see whether clip-ons work for you. It has less bass and detail than pricier pairs, but it is comfortable and loud enough for most conditions. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Nothing Ear (Open)** is SoundGuys' best open-ear pick overall. It has strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and about $99 pricing at Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Buying links:** The search results gave me a direct buy link only for the AeroFit 2. For the others, the review pages above link to retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, and Bose, and prices change often.

**My suggestion:** Pick the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 if you run in traffic or want maximum awareness. Pick the Bose or OpenDots 2 if you want a clip-on with better sound or battery. Start with the AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex if you're unsure about the style.

Keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you. Open-ear designs don't make running with headphones safe.
